name: aud.basic/intent/slurp
source: SLURP, test split, real recordings (Bastianelli et al., 2020)
license: audio CC BY-NC 4.0; annotations CC BY 4.0
criteria_source: Written; the options are SLURP's intent labels
notes: 500 utterances sampled round-robin over intents, one real recording each.

name: aud.basic/sound_event/sonyc_ust
source: SONYC-UST v2.3, test split, verified labels (Cartwright et al., 2020)
license: CC BY 4.0
criteria_source: Written; one yes/no question per SONYC-UST coarse class
notes: 500 ten-second recordings from 47 sensors of the SONYC urban sensor network, each with 8 questions, one per coarse class. Gold is the label the SONYC team agreed on (annotator_id 0). The test split is separated from the train split by time, not by sensor: its sensors also recorded the train and validate splits.

name: aud.basic/language_id/voxlingua107_dev
source: VoxLingua107, human-verified dev set (Valk and Alumäe, 2021)
license: CC BY 4.0; original copyright retained
criteria_source: Written; the options are the language codes of the dev set's 33 languages
notes: All 1,609 segments of the dev set, each confirmed by at least two volunteers. It covers 33 of VoxLingua107's 107 languages.

name: aud.basic/speaker_change/ami
source: AMI Meeting Corpus, Mix-Headset audio (Carletta et al., 2005)
license: CC BY 4.0; check AMI upstream conditions
criteria_source: Written; gold comes from AMI's word-level speaker alignment
notes: 500 clips of 1.3-2.3 s from 16 meetings: 250 with two adjacent, non-overlapping speaker turns, 250 with one speaker. Speaker boundaries come from the forced word alignment, not from manual frame-level labels. The question is whether the speaker changed within the clip, not whether to take the turn. Keep a meeting's clips together if you split the task.

name: aud.basic/acoustic_scene/tau2019
source: TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2019, development set, fold 1 evaluation subset (Mesaros et al., 2018)
license: TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2019 license (Tampere University): use and copying for non-commercial purposes, with its copyright notice in every copy; commercial use prohibited
criteria_source: Written; the options are the dataset's ten scene classes
notes: 50 ten-second clips per scene class, recorded at 141 locations in 10 cities; keep a location's clips together if you split the task. One scene label per clip. Not comparable with scores on other TAU editions.

name: aud.know/reasoning/mmau_mini
source: MMAU test-mini, v05.15.25 (Sakshi et al., 2025)
license: CC-BY-NC-4.0; underlying source terms apply
criteria_source: Original MMAU questions and options
notes: 330 speech questions. With aud.know/sound_qa and aud.know/music_understanding, a subset of test-mini that leaves out the questions on audio from some upstream datasets, so scores are not comparable with published test-mini results.

name: aud.know/reasoning/mmau_pro
source: MMAU-Pro, test set (Kumar et al., 2025)
license: CC-BY-NC-4.0 dataset; individual upstream audio lineage/terms not disclosed in selected metadata
notes: Not in this release: MMAU-Pro does not document where its audio comes from.

name: aud.know/sound_qa/mmau_mini
source: MMAU test-mini, v05.15.25 (Sakshi et al., 2025)
license: CC-BY-NC-4.0; underlying source terms apply
criteria_source: Original MMAU questions and options
notes: 36 sound questions, all on MMAU's synthetic audio. With aud.know/reasoning and aud.know/music_understanding, a subset of test-mini that leaves out the questions on audio from some upstream datasets, so scores are not comparable with published test-mini results.

name: aud.know/sound_qa/mmau_pro
source: MMAU-Pro, test set (Kumar et al., 2025)
license: CC-BY-NC-4.0 dataset; individual upstream audio lineage/terms not disclosed in selected metadata
notes: Not in this release: MMAU-Pro does not document where its audio comes from.

name: aud.know/music_understanding/mmau_mini
source: MMAU test-mini, v05.15.25 (Sakshi et al., 2025)
license: CC-BY-NC-4.0; underlying source terms apply
criteria_source: Original MMAU questions and options
notes: 105 music questions. With aud.know/reasoning and aud.know/sound_qa, a subset of test-mini that leaves out the questions on audio from some upstream datasets, so scores are not comparable with published test-mini results.

name: aud.know/music_understanding/mmau_pro
source: MMAU-Pro, test set (Kumar et al., 2025)
license: CC-BY-NC-4.0 dataset; individual upstream audio lineage/terms not disclosed in selected metadata
notes: Not in this release: MMAU-Pro does not document where its audio comes from.

name: aud.pro/machine_anomaly/mimii_pump_dcase2020
source: MIMII pump recordings, DCASE 2020 Challenge Task 2 development set (Purohit et al., 2019; Koizumi et al., 2020)
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (DCASE 2020 Task 2 development data, Zenodo 3678171)
criteria_source: Written; gold is the dataset's normal or anomalous label
notes: 500 ten-second clips of 4 pumps from the development set's test data (252 anomalous, 248 normal). Pumps only, not MIMII's other machine types. One label per clip, without anomaly onset times.

name: aud.pro/heart_sound/physionet2016
source: PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2016, validation set (Liu et al., 2016)
license: Open Data Commons Attribution v1.0; upstream content terms apply
criteria_source: Written; gold is the challenge's normal or abnormal label
notes: The 301 recordings of the validation set (151 abnormal, 150 normal), which are copies of training-set records. The respiratory task of this leaf asks a different question.

name: aud.pro/heart_sound/respiratory_icbhi2017
source: ICBHI 2017 Respiratory Sound Database, official test split, respiratory cycles (Rocha et al., 2019)
license: ICBHI 2017 Respiratory Sound Database: free for research use, citing Rocha et al. (2019); no license stated and no limit on redistribution
criteria_source: Written; the options combine the database's crackle and wheeze annotations of each cycle
notes: 500 respiratory cycles from 246 recordings of 40 patients of the official test split, without the patients who also appear in the train split; not the whole test split. Audio and cycle annotations come from a pinned public mirror of the database, not checked byte for byte against the official download. The heart-sound task of this leaf asks a different question.

name: aud.ret/audio_text_matching/sonyc_tag_descriptions
source: SONYC-UST v2.3, test split, verified labels (Cartwright et al., 2020)
license: CC BY 4.0
criteria_source: Written; template descriptions of the SONYC-UST coarse classes, e.g. 'An engine is audible.'
notes: 250 recordings, each asked with one matching and one non-matching description (250 yes, 250 no). The descriptions only say which coarse classes are audible, so this does not test free-form captions. The recordings are also in aud.basic/sound_event/sonyc_ust.

name: aud.dialog/turn_timing/full_duplex_bench_v1
source: Full-Duplex-Bench v1, CANDOR pause-handling and turn-taking samples (Lin et al., 2025; Reece et al., 2023)
license: Full-Duplex-Bench v1 annotations, CC BY-NC 4.0; audio from the CANDOR Corpus (BetterUp), not included: the CANDOR Corpus License lets a benchmark refer to it by id and timestamp, with labels (clause 4(a))
criteria_source: Written; gold comes from the benchmark's turn-taking and pause events
notes: 335 samples: 119 turn-taking events (take the turn) and 216 pauses (keep waiting). The audio ends at the decision point, with nothing after it. One label per sample, from its first event, not a distribution over annotators. The CANDOR conversation of each sample is not known, so do not split the task for training.

name: aud.dialog/dialogue_state/spokenwoz
source: SpokenWOZ, fixed test set (Si et al., 2023)
license: CC BY-NC 4.0
criteria_source: Written; gold is SpokenWOZ's dialogue state for four slots
notes: 500 dialogues, one item each, with four questions on closed slots: hotel parking, internet and price range, and restaurant area; not full dialogue state tracking. The audio runs from the start of the call to the end of the current user turn, without the next system turn.

name: aud.dialog/interrupt_backchannel/full_duplex_bench_v15
source: Full-Duplex-Bench v1.5, user interruption and backchannel samples (Lin et al., 2025)
license: MIT for synthetic v1.5 data
criteria_source: Written; gold is the benchmark's event type
notes: 200 interruptions and 98 backchannels (the download has 98, though the benchmark lists 99). The question gives the event's time span and asks which of the two it is, so this is not blind event detection or a closed-loop policy. Synthetic speech; the audio ends with the event, and the model is not given transcripts.

name: aud.judge/data_cleaning/nisqa_livetalk
source: NISQA Corpus, NISQA_TEST_LIVETALK (Mittag et al., 2021)
license: CC BY 4.0; original CC_BY_license.txt retained
criteria_source: Written; the quality options are the listening test's 5-point scale (1 Bad to 5 Excellent)
notes: 232 recordings of real phone and VoIP calls, each rated by 24 listeners; gold for both questions is the distribution of those ratings. keep_quality counts a rating of 4 or 5 as a keep, a threshold set for this benchmark, not a NISQA label; transcripts are not checked. Sentences recur across recordings and the speaker mapping is not published, so use the whole set for evaluation only.

name: aud.judge/data_cleaning/signal_defects_synthetic
source: SLURP test recordings with controlled signal defects (built for this benchmark)
license: derived audio CC BY-NC 4.0
criteria_source: Written; gold follows the silence and clipping rules stated in the question
notes: 436 recordings: 250 unchanged, 125 hard-clipped and 61 made silent. Gold is the rule in the question, not a listener rating; the leaf's other task, aud.judge/data_cleaning/nisqa_livetalk, uses listener ratings.

name: aud.judge/naturalness/bvcc
source: BVCC, VoiceMOS Challenge 2022 test set (Cooper and Yamagishi, 2021)
license: ratings BSD 3-Clause (Yamagishi Laboratory, NII); audio CC BY 4.0 (VCC 2016, 2018), ODbL 1.0 and DbCL (VCC 2020), public domain (ESPnet-TTS, from LJSpeech); no Blizzard Challenge samples
criteria_source: Written; the 5-point MOS scale of the listening test (1 Bad to 5 Excellent)
notes: 741 utterances of the test set, without its Blizzard Challenge samples, which BVCC does not redistribute; exact duplicate audio removed. Gold is the distribution of each utterance's 8 listener ratings.

name: aud.judge/caption_preference/fense_clotho
source: FENSE human caption preferences on Clotho evaluation audio (Zhou et al., 2022; Drossos et al., 2020)
license: Clotho per-file license and FENSE annotation terms; see provenance
notes: Not in this release. Caption pairs for Clotho evaluation audio with FENSE's human preferences; ties and vote distributions kept, caption order counterbalanced.

name: aud.safety/spoof_detection/asvspoof2019_la
source: ASVspoof 2019, Logical Access, evaluation split (Wang et al., 2020)
license: Open Data Commons Attribution; see original release content conditions
criteria_source: Written; gold is the official bona fide or spoof label
notes: 250 bona fide and 250 spoofed utterances from 67 speakers; the spoofs cover attacks A07-A19. Logical Access only (speech synthesis and voice conversion), without replay attacks. Attack and speaker ids are in meta.audio_provenance; the model gets only the audio.

name: aud.safety/toxicity/mutox
source: MuTox, English devtest (Costa-jussà et al., 2024)
license: MIT annotation release; individual podcast audio rights require review
criteria_source: Written; gold is MuTox's human toxicity label
notes: 167 segments (20 toxic, 147 not) whose source audio could still be downloaded and is marked public domain by its source: audiobooks on archive.org, 157 of them from LibriVox. A small subset with a strong source bias, not representative of MuTox's devtest. The public-domain mark is the source's own statement, recorded per item in meta.audio_provenance, not a legal guarantee.

name: aud.safety/injection/bipia_tts_twins
source: BIPIA email tasks (Yi et al., 2023) read aloud with Kokoro TTS (built for this benchmark)
license: BIPIA text MIT; Kokoro model Apache-2.0; kokoro-onnx MIT; preserve upstream notices
notes: A diagnostic task, not in the default suite; report it apart. BIPIA's 42 email texts (21 clean and attack pairs), read with one fixed Kokoro voice; pairs whose speech failed an ASR check (normalized WER above 0.25, or an error rate above 0.15 on the injected text) are left out. The check is lexical only.

name: aud.basic/emotion/cremad
source: CREMA-D, audio-only ratings (Cao et al., 2014)
license: ODbL / DbCL; see upstream license
criteria_source: Written; the options are CREMA-D's six emotions
notes: 1,470 clips of 18 of the 91 actors, held out by a speaker-disjoint split made for this benchmark (CREMA-D has no official split). Gold is the distribution of each clip's audio-only listener ratings (5 to 11 per clip); exact duplicate audio removed.
